key_insight: Cardiac-cycle-inspired pulsation suppresses turbulence during strong acceleration, while delayed turbulent shear recovery sustains a low-drag interval before turbulence rebounds.
engineering_relevance: Phase-resolved turbulence dynamics can inform pulsatile pipe-flow strategies that seek to manage drag through waveform timing and low-flow plateaus.
method: Direct numerical simulations of four pulsatile pipe-flow cases across two Reynolds-number ranges.
Comparison of waveforms with and without a low-flow plateau.
Phase-resolved analysis of turbulent stresses, streak disturbances, momentum transport and friction.
evidence_signal: Across the simulated cases, stress production recovers ahead of redistribution and radial transport, while a low-flow plateau prolongs turbulence decay and delays local instability.
watch_item: Findings are limited to the simulated pipe-flow waveforms and Reynolds-number ranges; broader operating conditions require validation.
paper_title: Phase-resolved turbulence dynamics in cardiac-cycle-inspired pulsatile pipe flow
